title: Garments of skin and garments of light: letters that break and letters that hold
overview:
G-d made Adam and his wife garments of skin; in Rabbi Meir's Torah they were garments of light. The chapter explains the difference through the letters. In *Tohu* the letters, the vessels, could not hold their great light: they crumbled and scattered, as a big idea told to someone who cannot hold it turns into nonsense, as a word too small for its meaning becomes a jumble, and as a dream mixes up the day's thoughts. Crumb after crumb, the true idea becomes its opposite. The fallen letters became the *chashmal*, the garments of thought, speech and action that surround a person's *middos* and guard them, rooted above *bina*.

Yet the letters are also the only way to grasp a light: a light not in letters cannot be felt, and "He can only be experienced" is a very big mistake. A deep wisdom is grasped only in a *mashal*, whose root is above the *nimshal*. Taken literally, the *mashal* is skin that covers; understood, it is light that clarifies. Rabbi Markel reads this as the work of *Moshiach ben Yosef* and of this book: putting the *Aibershter* into 78 pages.

terms.gloss: the garment of letters, of thought, speech and action, that surrounds the middos; separate, yet rooted above bina
garments of skin: the chashmal as it comes from the breaking, covering what it clothes; with an alef, garments of light, which clarify
the breaking of the vessels: letters too small for their light, crumbled and scattered
confusion; what an idea becomes when its letters cannot hold it
(Yiddish) taken in: the light held and settled in the letters
an elephant through the eye of a needle: the thing too big for the small one, seen only in a nightmare
a separate garment: the chashmal, which can stand apart from the intellect
the outside of bina: where an idea comes into the letters of an explanation, the root of the chashmal
a mashal on a mashal; in the last and most physical one is the deepest source of the nimshal
an interpreter of dreams, who puts the scattered letters back in order: Yosef

sections.title: Garments of skin, and in Rabbi Meir's Torah garments of light
sections.summary: The garments of skin G-d made for Adam and his wife are the *chashmal* of *noga* that surrounds *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*. Rabbi Meir's Torah wrote them with an *alef*, garments of light, because by him the Torah was already past the sorting.

phrases.he: (מה) והנה כתיב ויעש יהו״ה לאדם ולאשתו כתנות עור וילבישם
שזהו בחינת החשמ"ל דנוגה שמקיף לזעיר אנפין ונוקבא דאצילות שנקרא אדם ואשתו עד מתחת רגליהם כו' כידוע
ובתורתו של רבי מאיר היה כתוב אור באלף
שזהו בחינת זיהרא עילאה, כמו שכתוב עוטה אור כשלמה,
שזהו אחר הבירורים דרפ"ח כו'.
phrases.en: by him the Torah was already after the *birurim*.

blocks.text: G-d made Adam and his wife garments of skin, *kosnos or* (with an *ayin*), and clothed them. That is the *chashmal* (the garment of letters) of *noga*, which surrounds *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* of *Atzilus*, called Adam and his wife, down to below their feet. In Rabbi Meir's Torah *or* was written with an *alef*, light: the higher radiance of "He wraps Himself in light as a garment", which comes after the *birurim* (sortings). In other words, **by him the Torah was already after the *birurim***.

sections.title: The breaking: an idea with too much light for its letters
sections.summary: The letters are the vessels, and in *Tohu* they broke because the light was too much for them, as a big idea told to one who cannot hold it crumbles into nonsense. When the letters do hold the light the idea settles and is taken in, and to know the *Aibershter* at all it has to be in letters.

phrases.he: ומתחלה יש להבין קצת בביאור ענין השבירה והתיקון בכללותן
phrases.en: so now we have to understand the *inyan* of the *shevira* and the *Tikkun*,

phrases.he: שהוא בבחינת האותיות שנקרא כלים
שנשברו ונפלו מצד ריבוי האור שלא היה ביכולתם להכיל
phrases.en: Because there was too much light, the *kelim* couldn't hold it,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בעץ חיים
phrases.en: like it says in *Etz Chaim*.

blocks.text: Now we have to understand the *shevira* (breaking) and the *Tikkun* (repair) in general. The letters are called the vessels, *kelim*, and they broke and fell because there was too much light for them to hold. Tell somebody an idea too high for him, too big, with too much light, and it breaks apart into a bunch of nonsense.

The perfect example is *Chassidus*. Look on the internet and see what happened with *Kabbala* and *Chassidus*: they turned it worse than upside down, into total nonsense. People outside, like the Berg people or the Hermetic people, tried to study these kabbalistic things, and since the idea had too much light in it, it broke up into nonsense.

sensitivity.reason: Names present-day groups ("the Berg people", the family behind a popular Kabbala center, and the Hermetic people) as having turned Kabbala into nonsense.
sensitivity.publishable: The perfect example is *Chassidus*. Look on the internet and see what happened with *Kabbala* and *Chassidus*: they turned it worse than upside down, into total nonsense. People outside tried to study these kabbalistic things, and since the idea had too much light in it, it broke up into nonsense.

blocks.title: Boiling water and hammering a nail
blocks.text: That is the basic thing of the *shevira*: there was too much light, the *kelim* could not hold it, so they broke up. A small idea without much light, like how to boil water (put it on the fire and wait till it bubbles) or how to hammer a nail, will not break up. By some people even that will break up; but by most people there is not that much light in it.

blocks.title: Art Linkletter's kids
blocks.text: When the idea gets very big, it gets mixed up. Little kids in the first grades are taught history or mathematics, and on the shows of the funny things kids say, like Art Linkletter's, they come out with all kinds of mix-ups: when they first learn it, the idea is too big for them. That is the *inyan* here. **Because there was too much light, the *kelim* couldn't hold it**.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב אתה פוררת בעזך ים
phrases.en: You crumbled up the ocean.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת התהו, שנתפררו בחינת האותיות,
phrases.en: that the letters got all separated out.

phrases.he: שנקרא שבירת הכלים כידוע
phrases.en: and this is what's called *sheviras hakelim*.

blocks.text: As the verse says, *Ata forarta b'azcha yam*. The sea is *Malchus*, speech: the words got mixed up. This is *Tohu*, **that the letters got all separated out**. *Pirurim* are crumbs, what a little kid makes of bread or a cookie when he crumbles it up. **You crumbled up the ocean**, and this is what's called *sheviras hakelim* (the breaking of the vessels).

phrases.he: וטעם הדבר ידוע, על דרך משל עומק אור שכל שלמעלה מכלי הגבלת המוח, אז ודאי יתבלבלו אותיות השכל שבמחשבה,
phrases.en: when there is a very big idea that's higher than the brain being able to contain it, the letters of thought get mixed up.

phrases.he: מצד מיעוט כחם להכיל האור,
phrases.en: It all becomes a big *bilbul*, because he can't hold it in the words of the *sechel*,

phrases.he: כי רב הוא מהם
phrases.en: because the light is too much for them to hold.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן כלי המוח שמכיל לאור השכל העמוק, אדרבא
phrases.en: So, when the letters actually do contain the *sechel*, it's just the opposite.

phrases.he: מוגבל ומתיישב ונעלם באותיות הללו
phrases.en: Then the *sechel* really becomes *misyashev*, *davka* through the *osios*.

phrases.he: (בלשון אידייש פאר נעמט כו')
phrases.en: *farnemt* means gets taken in. It is taken in by the letters.

phrases.he: וכאשר לא יכילו,
phrases.en: but when the letters don't contain the light,

phrases.he: אזי בהכרח שיתפרדו האותיות
phrases.en: then they have to basically get separate; in other words, it explodes.

blocks.text: The reason: when an idea is very big, higher than the brain's vessel can contain, the letters of thought are certainly mixed up. **It all becomes a big *bilbul*** (confusion), because he cannot hold it in the words of the *sechel* (intellect): **the light is too much for them to hold**.

But where the vessels of the brain do contain the deep light of the *sechel*, **it's just the opposite**. **Then the *sechel* really becomes *misyashev*** (settled), *davka* (precisely) through the letters. One might have thought that a *sechel* this big, since it gets mixed up, cannot be put in letters at all.

blocks.title: Chassidus is about the Aibershter, not the chain of worlds
blocks.text: What we are learning is G-dliness. *Chassidus* is not really about the *seder hishtalshelus* (the chain of worlds); *Kabbala* is. As the Rebbe's famous talk *Inyana shel Toras HaChassidus* says, the subject of *Chassidus* is G-d Himself, not the chain. Here it is a *mashal* on a *mashal* on a *mashal*, until the subject of *Kabbala* itself becomes a *mashal*. That is why we started before the *tzimtzum*: *Kabbala* does not start before the *tzimtzum*, and here we are really talking about the *Aibershter*.

blocks.question: Isn't the Aibershter such a big light that He cannot be contained in words?
blocks.text: Everybody claims this, and *l'havdil* all the *goyishkeit* (the non-Jewish world) says He can only be experienced, not said. The text says this is a very big mistake. A light not contained in letters cannot be felt; then a person is like a dog, with no actual *daas*. That is no *daas* of *Havaya*. To know the *Aibershter*, or anything, it has to be *davka* in letters, and then it is the opposite: it is *mugbal*, held.

sensitivity.reason: Likens one who seeks to experience G-d without letters, as non-Jewish mysticism teaches, to a dog.
sensitivity.publishable: Everybody claims this, and *l'havdil* all the *goyishkeit* (the non-Jewish world) says He can only be experienced, not said. The text says this is a very big mistake. A light not contained in letters cannot be felt; then a person has no actual *daas*. That is no *daas* of *Havaya*. To know the *Aibershter*, or anything, it has to be *davka* in letters, and then it is the opposite: it is *mugbal*, held.

blocks.text: *Farnemt* (Yiddish) means taken in: **it is taken in by the letters**. More than that, the person takes it into himself *davka* through the letters, not by way of direct *chachma*. That was the mistake spoken of in chapter one, to have *daas* go straight into *chachma*. Their reason is that the divided letters of *bina* cannot accept so high a light; and here he says *adraba*, just the opposite: *davka* when you take it into letters you can take it in, and otherwise you cannot.
**But when the letters don't contain the light**, they have to separate: it explodes. Instead of a *yishuv* (settling), the whole thing becomes a big *bilbul*.

Being put into letters makes an even bigger *bilbul* than not being put into letters. A simple guy who just says "There's a G-d in the world", with simple *emuna* in the *Aibershter*, who knows he has to keep the *mitzvos* and be a good Jew and never tries to put these things into words, has no *bilbul*, though of course he does not have it in a deeper way. It is *davka* those who try to get it deeper, studying the *Zohar* and such, by whom there is a fantastic *bilbul*: the Hermetic kabbalists, or the people who go to the book center.

sensitivity.reason: Singles out present-day groups that study Kabbala (the Hermetic kabbalists, the people at "the book center") as being in a great confusion.
sensitivity.publishable: Being put into letters makes an even bigger *bilbul* than not being put into letters. A simple guy who just says "There's a G-d in the world", with simple *emuna* in the *Aibershter*, who knows he has to keep the *mitzvos* and be a good Jew and never tries to put these things into words, has no *bilbul*, though of course he does not have it in a deeper way. It is *davka* those who try to get it deeper, studying the *Zohar* and such, by whom there is a fantastic *bilbul*.

blocks.text: That was the whole thing with Shabsai Tzvi, and with the Frankists. As long as everybody stayed with just doing the *halacha*, being a good boy and not trying to understand too much, everything was fine. Whenever people went into the deeper dimension of the Torah, it almost invariably ended in a big *bilbul*.

This book contains the *Atzmus* (essence) of the *Or Ein Sof*, *mamash* the *Atzmus*, in its letters. "These letters" in the text are these: this book *farnemt*, takes in, the *yichud* (unity) of the *Aibershter*. Elsewhere the light was too big to be contained, and they exploded, as the world of *Tohu* exploded.

sections.title: A word that cannot hold its meaning: crumbs, jumbles and dreams
sections.summary: A word too small for its meaning scatters its letters until nothing is understood, like the jumbled letters of a dream. Each crumb carries only a sliver of the idea, and crumb after crumb it turns into the opposite of what was meant; yet even a dream is made of the day's thoughts, and an elephant through a needle's eye comes only in a nightmare.

phrases.he: וכמו שמבואר במקום אחר באריכות, שזהו כמו בתיבה אחת שתקצר להכיל האור הרב שבה,
יתפרדו האותיות שבה אנה ואנה, עד שלא יהיה מובן מזה כלום
phrases.en: It'll become a *bilbul* till you don't understand nothing from it.

phrases.he: כתיבת ויאמר כשלא יכיל עומק המכוון שבו,
phrases.en: when it will not be able to contain the *omek* which is *mechuvan* in it,

phrases.he: יתפרדו האותיות, וישאר וי"ו מ״ם שבו מפורדין שלא כסדרן במקומן

blocks.text: When the letters cannot contain the light, they must separate. A single word too short for the great light in it scatters its letters here and there: **It'll become a *bilbul* till you don't understand nothing from it**. So with the word *vayomer*, when it cannot hold the depth intended in it: a *vav* here and a *yud* there, out of order, and you have no idea what it means.

phrases.he: (כדוגמת אותיות הרהורי לבו שביום, שמתפרדין שלא במקומן ושלא כסדרן בחלומות
שבאין רק מצרופים שמהרהר ביום, בלתי מסודרין, אלא אות מתיבה זו ואות מתיבה אחרת כו'
ולכך החלומות שוא ידברו
phrases.en: And that's why the *chalomos* talk about nonsense,

phrases.he: כו' וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר)

blocks.text: It is like the letters of the day's thoughts, which in dreams come apart, out of place and out of order. So it says, *B'shuv Hashem es shivas Tzion hayinu k'cholmim*: the *golus* (exile) is likened to a dream, where all the letters are there and everything is mixed up.

A dream comes only from combinations thought of during the day, in no order, a letter from this word and a letter from that one, like the jumbles they have. **And that's why the *chalomos* talk about nonsense**, unless you know how to put the letters back together properly, as a *poser chalomos* (interpreter of dreams) does.

phrases.he: וזה הפירור
phrases.en: this crumbling,

phrases.he: נקרא שבירה לחלקים רבים וקטנים
phrases.en: It breaks it up into a bunch of little pieces.

phrases.he: כי בבוא זה האות שנתפרר לעצמו במקום אחר,
phrases.en: when this particular thing that got crumbled up comes in another place,

phrases.he: אין בו רק חלק מצומצם מאד מן השכל שהיה מקובץ בהיות התיבה בצירופה בשלימות כו'
וגם הוא מתפרר
פירור אחר פירור, עד שנעשה מזה ענין זר לגמרי
phrases.en: It all becomes a whole total opposite thing.

blocks.text: And **this crumbling** is what is called a breaking into many small parts. **It breaks it up into a bunch of little pieces**.

This is how people understand *Chassidus*: not as a coherent whole, but as a bunch of little points, a point here and a point there, with no idea how the points go together. That is what is called *olam hanekudos*, the world of points.

So **when this particular thing that got crumbled up comes in another place**, it holds only a tiny part of the *sechel* that was gathered in the whole word. And it crumbles again, crumb after crumb. **It all becomes a whole total opposite thing**. That is the real *inyan* of *sheviras hakelim*: the original idea is the correct one, but crumb after crumb it turned into the opposite of the original *kavana* (intent).

phrases.he: (כדוגמת ענין החלומות מהרהורי לבו שביום,
רק אף על פי כן לא יחלום פילא בקופא דמחטא,
phrases.en: But nonetheless, he's not going to think of an elephant going through the eye of a needle.

phrases.he: רק מעין הרהורי לבו דוקא,
phrases.en: But it'll be just like the *hirhurei liba davka*.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין פותר חלומות דיוסף וכמו שיתבאר)

blocks.text: Dreams are made of the thoughts of the day. Even so, **he's not going to think of an elephant going through the eye of a needle**: what he dreams is just like the *hirhurei liba* (the thoughts of his heart).

blocks.title: The elephant through the eye of a needle
blocks.text: The Frierdiker Rebbe asks in a *maamar* (he first says 5668, then that he does not remember the year: it is *Balayla hahu nadda shnas hamelech*) where you can have a *pila b'kufa d'machta*, an elephant through the eye of a needle. Only in a dream, and not a regular dream, where, as the text says here, you cannot have it, but a total nightmare, something totally crazy. And it explains that the whole reason for the *golus*, why it got to such a crazy point, and why the king had to sleep, is to have this *pila b'kufa d'machta*.

By the way, the *pila b'kufa d'machta* is very much the *sheviras hakelim*: fit an elephant through the eye of a needle and it blows it up, as the *shevira* comes when the light is too big for the *kli*. But there are two *inyanim*: a light too big cannot be contained, yet *davka* when it is contained in letters it becomes *misgashem* (embodied); so the elephant does go through, in a dream. And that is the whole *inyan* of this book: you are putting the *Aibershter* into 78 pages.

sections.title: The letters of Tohu fall and become the garment of chashmal
sections.summary: The lights of *Tohu* did not break; their letters scattered and fell until they became a foreign garment, the *chashmal*, the garments of skin, which surround a person's *middos*. Separate as it is, its root is higher than *bina*'s source of the *mochin*, in the outside of *bina* and its encompassing light.

phrases.he: וכך יובן למעלה בענין שבירת הכלים דאורות דתהו, שזהו בחינת פירור ופיזור האותיות שלהם, כמו שכתוב אתה פוררת כו'

blocks.text: So it is above, in the breaking of the vessels of the lights of *Tohu*. The lights of *Tohu* did not break; they just went back up. They are true lights, true holy lights. The trouble was that they were too big for the *kelim*, so the letters were scattered every which way, until finally it ended in witchcraft and *avoda zara* (idol worship) and all kinds of things.

phrases.he: והיינו שנפלו למטה מטה
phrases.en: because they got mixed up they fell farther and farther down,

phrases.he: עד שנעשה בבחינת לבוש זר
phrases.en: until it became into total *schmutz*.

phrases.he: שזהו שרש ענין התהוות בחינת לבוש דחשמל כו'
phrases.en: this is the *shoresh* of the coming into being of the *levush* of *chashmal*,

phrases.he: הנקרא כתנות עור

blocks.text: That is, **because they got mixed up they fell farther and farther down**, until they became a foreign garment, **total *schmutz***. And **this is the *shoresh* of the coming into being of the *levush* of *chashmal***, the garment called *kosnos or*, garments of skin.

phrases.he: וידוע דעור זה הן בחינת ג' מיני אותיות דמחשבה דבור ומעשה, ששרשם הוא מאותיות דכלים דתהו שנתפררו וירדו למטה,
ונעשה בחינת לבוש ומקיף להלביש לבחינת המדות דאדם כו'
phrases.en: until the *middos* of *adam* are *malbush* with these *levushei chashmal*.

blocks.text: The skin is the three kinds of letters, of thought, speech and action, rooted in the scattered letters of the vessels of *Tohu*, which came down and became a garment around a person's *middos* (character traits): **until the *middos* of *adam* are *malbush* with these *levushei chashmal***. People's characters are made up of these mistaken ideas.

Some are made up wholly of these broken letters of *Tohu*, like the terrorists or the Palestinians: it is their whole idea of life. This is the basic *inyan* of the breaking of *Tohu*. The real *Tohu* you see right here, right now.

sensitivity.reason: Names the Palestinians, beside terrorists, as made up wholly of the broken letters of Tohu.
sensitivity.publishable: Some are made up wholly of these broken letters of *Tohu*: it is their whole idea of life. This is the basic *inyan* of the breaking of *Tohu*. The real *Tohu* you see right here, right now.

blocks.text: And these letters of *chashmal* are what the talk of demons is about, demons making wars and making things happen. There are demons running around putting ideas in Palestinians' heads, and they are made of *chashmal*, made up of letters. They actually have a *partzuf*, a whole stature of ten *sefiros*. So how, in the old days, could some people see what the demons looked like? It is like what he heard on a CD he was given: in the letters of the DNA you can see what a person looks like. So there are actual demons running around whispering in these *meshugene* Arabs' ears to go and blow things up, and they are made of *chashmal*, from the breaking of the vessels of *Tohu*.

sensitivity.reason: Says demons put ideas in Palestinians' heads and whisper in "these meshugene Arabs'" ears to blow things up.
sensitivity.publishable: And these letters of *chashmal* are what the talk of demons is about, demons making wars and making things happen. There are demons running around putting ideas in people's heads, and they are made of *chashmal*, made up of letters. They actually have a *partzuf*, a whole stature of ten *sefiros*. So how, in the old days, could some people see what the demons looked like? It is like what he heard on a CD he was given: in the letters of the DNA you can see what a person looks like. So there are actual demons running around whispering in people's ears to go and do harm, and they are made of *chashmal*, from the breaking of the vessels of *Tohu*.

blocks.text: So this *chashmal*, from the breaking of the three letters of thought, speech and action, becomes the *makifim* (encompassing garments) around a person's *middos*: it makes up characteristics, as with Edom and Moav. When the *Aibershter* came to give them the Torah, by Edom it was murder, by Moav lust, by Yishmael stealing, "something like that".

phrases.he: וגם שהוא נעשה בבחינת לבוש נפרד,
phrases.en: even though this *chashmal* is a *levush nifrad*,

phrases.he: שרשו מלמעלה ממקור המוחין דבינה שבמדות
phrases.en: the *shoresh* of it is higher than the *makor* of the *mochin* of *bina* and the *middos*.

phrases.he: וזהו גם כן בחינת חיצוניות בינה,
phrases.en: This is also the *shoresh* of it, in *chitzoniyus bina*.

phrases.he: שעל גוזליו ירחף לשמירה כו',
שהוא מבחינת המקיף דבינה בבחינת מ"ם סתומה הנזכר לעיל ודי למבין.
phrases.en: this external of *bina* really has a *shoresh* in the *makif* of *bina* and the *mem stuma*.

blocks.text: And **even though this *chashmal* is a *levush nifrad*** (a separate garment), **the *shoresh* of it is higher than the *makor* of the *mochin* of *bina* and the *middos***: its root is above the source of the intellect of *bina* that is in the *middos*.

**This is also the *shoresh* of it, in *chitzoniyus bina*** (the outside of *bina*), which "hovers over its young" to guard them. It comes from the *uvchein* ("and so") of *bina* when it comes into the *middos*: "so therefore I like him", or "therefore I hate him". Then the *uvchein* takes on a life of its own. But really it has a root even higher than *bina* and the *makifim* of *bina* themselves.

And **this external of *bina* really has a *shoresh* in the *makif* of *bina* and the *mem stuma***, the closed *mem*, locked and sealed. In other words, the *chashmal* is really higher than the *mochin* altogether.

sections.title: The mashal comes from above the nimshal
sections.summary: A deep wisdom cannot be said in its own letters; it is grasped only dressed in a *mashal* far from it, and whoever makes a *mashal* that fits must know the *nimshal* at its source and above. Taken literally, a *mashal* breaks into idolatry; and the further down an idea is explained, through letters and explanations, the deeper its source.

phrases.he: ולהבין זה בתוספת ביאור, הנה ידוע שזהו גם כן שרש ענין המשלים,
phrases.en: this is also the *inyan* of the *mashal*,

phrases.he: כמו ג' מאות משלים דרבי מאיר כו', ששרש המשל למעלה מן הנמשל, כמו משלי שלמה שהן חכמות עמוקות ביותר

blocks.text: To explain this further: **this is also the *inyan* of the *mashal***, as in the three hundred *meshalim* of Rabbi Meir, whose root is above the *nimshal* (what it stands for), like the *Mishlei* of Shlomo, the deepest wisdom. He thinks the three hundred allegories of Rabbi Meir are the three worlds, *Beriya, Yetzira and Asiya*, and the three thousand are up in *Atzilus* already.

phrases.he: שאין להם בחינת כלים באותיות
phrases.en: you cannot just put the *sechel* into a *kli*, just in letters, to say the thing itself, this *chachma* itself.

phrases.he: כי אם בהתלבשותם בענינים זרים נבדלים הרבה מן עצם החכמה,
phrases.en: *davka* when you enclothe it in a totally different thing that's separate from the *etzem hachachma*,

phrases.he: שם דוקא יושג עומק החכמה כמו שיוכלו להשיג עומק השכל
רק על ידי המשל דוקא, שלא יושג גם ברבוי הסבר דברים כו'
phrases.en: even if you explain it and explain it, you couldn't explain it, and *davka* through the *mashal*.

blocks.text: Such wisdom has no vessel in letters: **you cannot just put the *sechel* into a *kli***, saying the thing itself in words. Only **when you enclothe it in a totally different thing that's separate from the *etzem hachachma*** (the wisdom itself), like a *mashal* from the physical world, is the depth of the wisdom grasped. However you try, **even if you explain it and explain it, you couldn't explain it**: only through the *mashal*.

phrases.he: והמשל שנעשה לפי אופן הנמשל דוקא,
phrases.en: In order to come up with a *mashal gashmi* that is according to the *ofen hanimshal*,

phrases.he: הרי בהכרח שישיג לעומק ומקור מוצא הנמשל,
phrases.en: he has to understand the *omek* and *makor* of the *nimshal*.

phrases.he: ואם לא, לא יכוון המשל לנמשל כלל כידוע
phrases.en: then the *mashal* will not be able to be *mechuvan* properly to the *nimshal*.

phrases.he: אם כן שרש המשל במקור שכל הנמשל
phrases.en: So therefore the *shoresh hamashal* is in the *makor* of the *sechel hanimshal*,

phrases.he: ולמעלה הימנו
phrases.en: Not only that, it's really higher than it,

blocks.text: **In order to come up with a *mashal gashmi* that is according to the *ofen hanimshal*** (a physical *mashal* that fits the way of the *nimshal*), **he has to understand the *omek* and *makor* of the *nimshal*** better than one who understands the *nimshal* itself, or the *mashal* will not fit. So the root of the *mashal* is in the source of the *nimshal*. **Not only that, it's really higher than it**: one may understand that source and still not be able to make a *mashal*. *Davka* Shlomo could; he is even smarter.

phrases.he: ולזה אמר דברי חכמים וחידותם,
phrases.en: like their riddles, riddles or *meshalim*.

phrases.he: שלפי ערך עומק ומקור החכמה, כך ערך החידות ומשלים, כמו משלים דרבי מאיר ומשלי שלמה
וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין וידבר ג' אלפים משל, דהיינו משל למשל,
phrases.en: not 3,000 different *meshalim*, but a *mashal* on a *mashal* 3,000 times,

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בזהר שהנמצא במשל האחרון,
phrases.en: that you see that in the final *mashal*, which is totally *megusham*,

phrases.he: יותר שם הוא העומק והמקור היותר ראשון של הנמשל כו'
phrases.en: *davka* there it's higher than even the depth of the *nimshal* itself.

blocks.text: "The words of the wise and their riddles": **like their riddles, riddles or *meshalim***. As deep as the source of the wisdom, so deep are its riddles and *meshalim*. Shlomo "spoke three thousand *meshalim*": **not 3,000 different *meshalim*, but a *mashal* on a *mashal* 3,000 times**, *mashal l'mashal*, so that in the last, most *megusham* (physical) *mashal*, **it's higher than even the depth of the *nimshal* itself**.

By the way, the *shevira* also comes from *meshalim*, when somebody takes the *mashal* literally and does not realize it is a *mashal*. That is what happened with *avoda zara*: the cow and such; G-d as a father, a father and a mother; it says "a sun and a shield", so they started praying to the sun.
Even now, the Eastern religions actually think it means a light: they talk of a white light or something like that.

sensitivity.reason: Says the Eastern religions take the mashal of light literally.
sensitivity.publishable: Even now, some actually think it means a light: they talk of a white light or something like that.

blocks.text: But it does not mean a light. Even *or hachachma*, the light of wisdom, is not a light like this light; anybody understands that. Yet when people hear *Or Ein Sof* they literally think of a light from a very big light bulb: not a regular bulb, a sodium bulb, like the street lights. Most people think it *mamash* means light.

They do not realize that even "spiritual" does not mean spiritual: the *Aibershter* is not spiritual like the spirit in the body. It's a *mashal*. This is the *mashal l'mashal*: as the *Zohar* explains, in the furthest *mashal* is the deepest source.

phrases.he: וכל זה הוא גם כן בשרש בחינת האותיות,
phrases.en: The same thing in the *shoresh* of *bechinas ha'osios*.

phrases.he: שעל ידיהם דוקא יושג היטב אור השכל כו'
phrases.en: that *davka* through the *osios* and explanations, the depth of the light of the *sechel* will be understood.

phrases.he: (וכמו כן יובן בענין ההגשמה של אור השכל, כל שבא בהשגה והסבר בהגשמה ביותר למטה מטה, שם דוקא בחינת העומק והמקור של גוף פנימית אור השכל כו')

blocks.text: **The same thing in the *shoresh* of *bechinas ha'osios***, the root of the letters: **that *davka* through the *osios* and explanations, the depth of the light of the *sechel* will be understood**. That is the basic point of the *perushim* (explanations) of *Moshiach*: *davka* through them the infinite light will be grasped.

So too the embodiment of the light of the intellect: whatever is grasped and explained in the most physical way, furthest down, there is the depth and source of its inner light. The farther down someone can explain it, the more it shows how smart he is: to explain it farther down, he had to understand it farther up.

sections.title: The guard over the middos, and garments of skin that become garments of light
sections.summary: The outside of *bina* brings an idea into the letters of an explanation, where it can stand apart from the intellect: the garment of *chashmal*, a guard that keeps the *middos* from error, and the placenta, a *kelipa*. Taken literally a *mashal* covers its meaning; seen as a *mashal* it lights it up, and the garments of skin become garments of light, the work of *Moshiach ben Yosef* and of this book.

phrases.he: והיינו גם כן בחינת חיצוניות בינה,
phrases.en: And this is also what is called the *chitzoniyus* of *bina*.

phrases.he: שמזה נעשה בחינת לבוש החשמל דבינה
phrases.en: meaning that when this explanation becomes an explanation, it can become a separated thing out from the actual *sechel*.

phrases.he: שעל זה אמר ויעש כתנות עור כו', שהוא בחינת שומר למוחין שבמדות, שלא יבא לבחינת טעות

blocks.text: **And this is also what is called the *chitzoniyus* of *bina***: from it the thing comes, through the *Malchus* of *tevuna*, into the letters of an actual explanation. From it is made the garment of the *chashmal* of *bina*: **when this explanation becomes an explanation, it can become a separated thing out from the actual *sechel***, put into letters so that you can *mamash* write it down. Like this book: it is written down, it is a *chashmal*.

This is "He made garments of skin", and the garments of skin come *davka* from the *shevira*. They are a guard for the *mochin* in the *middos*, so that they do not come to error. Once a person has the *uvchein*, it becomes the *mochin* for the *middos*: he knows he likes this thing, and that keeps the *midda*. He does not have to go through the whole *hisbonenus* (contemplation); he made the decision that he likes it, and that is the *mochin* for the *midda*.

phrases.he: (שמזה נעשה השליא לולד כו')
phrases.en: And this is like the placenta for a baby.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר באריכות בענין אימא פרישת גדפהא כו' ובענין בשלו״ם, אותיות מלבו״ש כו', ובענין סכך דסוכה וכהאי גוונא ודי למבין

blocks.text: From this comes the placenta for the child. **And this is like the placenta for a baby**: it is a *kelipa*, the general *inyan* of the *kelipos*. But when it comes into *Tikkun* it becomes *kosnos or* with an *alef*, garments of light: not only does it not cover up, it actually makes things clear.

blocks.question: So the mashal still remains, and now the nimshal shines in the mashal?
blocks.text: The garment is still there, and a *mashal* can be two things. Take it for the actual thing and it is garments of skin: it covers up the *nimshal*, and you pray to the sun. Understand that it is a *mashal*, not the sun's actual light, and *davka* through it you see the *nimshal*: garments of light, with an *alef*. He thinks the next chapter speaks of this, the *aspaklaria hameira* (the clear lens).
The text then points to other places in *Kabbala* that speak of these *inyanim*: *Imma* spreading her wings, *shalom* with the letters of *malbush* (garment), the *schach* of the *sukka*.

So the basic thing is this. When the letters do not hold the *sechel*, they break up, it becomes a big *bilbul*, and that is *Tohu*. When the letters do hold the *sechel*, *davka* then the *sechel* is settled, and *davka* through the letters you can get it.

This is how, as he will explain later, the *golus* will be straightened out. The *golus* is like a dream with a big *bilbul*, and then comes Yosef the *poser chalomos*, who says what goes where and gives the dream its meaning. They said that the Mitteler Rebbe was *Moshiach ben Yosef*, Yosef who interprets the dreams; and that is what we are doing, putting all these things in order.

This chapter is very apropos for right now: it is about *Moshiach ben Yosef* and how he is going to take over the world, by changing the *tzerufim* (combinations of letters). *Tohu* was that the *kelim* did not hold the light; the Rebbe spoke of the lights of *Tohu* in the vessels of *Tikkun*, and the main place of that is this book, which holds fantastic lights. The real lights of *Tohu* are not even the lights of *Tohu*: they are the lights from before the *tzimtzum*, coming in without a *tzimtzum*, and that breaks everything. The whole creation was to reach the point where *davka* those lights can come in and be held, in the *kelim* of *Tikkun*, which are the letters of the Torah.

The Torah was given at first as smaller lights in very heavy vessels: the revealed Torah, *halacha*, which just tells you what to do. The teaching of *Moshiach* is that once these *kelim* are very strong, the original lights can come into them. That is this book, which explains that the *tzimtzum* is not *kipshuto* (literal), as a teacher starts children with small things to reach the big ones. What comes next is how the garments of skin change from an *ayin* to an *alef*.

reviewQuestions.question: Why did the vessels of Tohu break, and what happens to an idea too big for the one who hears it?
Why does a light held in letters settle instead of breaking, and what is wrong with saying G-d can only be experienced?
How is a crumbled word like a dream, and what can a dream not show?
Where is the root of the chashmal, and how does the uvchein of bina take on a life of its own?
Why must one who makes a mashal know the nimshal better than one who only knows the nimshal?
When is a mashal a garment of skin and when a garment of light?
